extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, journalists, and Wikipedia editors interested in the East Palestine derailment or railway incident coverage
extracted.subtask_description: Encyclopedic article documenting a transportation/chemical incident, including timeline, causes, response, impacts, investigations, and sources. Geared toward comprehensive, neutrally worded coverage suitable for Wikipedia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infobox / incident details
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise top-of-article summary (infobox) including date, time, location, coordinates, country, operator, incident type, cause, and key statistics (deaths, injured).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include precise values (dates/times, coordinates), the operator, a short statement of cause if known (e.g., 'Defective wheel bearing that overheated'), and high-level statistics; support all facts with citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the train's origin, route, operator, consist (locomotives and cars), cargo (including hazardous materials), crew composition, prior mechanical issues, and relevant operational context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List train number, yards of origin/destination, length/weight, number and type of cars (e.g., hazardous-material tank cars), and cite official reports or contemporaneous sources when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derailment — sequence and immediate facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the time and place of the derailment, the number of cars derailed, which cars contained hazardous materials, eyewitness and surveillance evidence (e.g., video, Ring footage), and preliminary investigative findings (e.g., hotbox detector alarms, overheated bearing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include NTSB preliminary findings if available, witness accounts, and technical details about sensors/alarms; cite authoritative investigative sources and avoid speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency response and controlled burn description
rubrics_metrics.description: Document emergency agencies involved, declarations of emergency, evacuation zones, actions taken (booms, dams, booms, controlled release and burn), consultation with agencies (EPA), and timeline of response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain rationale for major actions (e.g., vent and burn), note which agencies were consulted, describe monitoring conducted (air, water), and include monitoring results; attribute contested decisions to sources (e.g., NTSB testimony).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental and health impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover documented environmental damage (fish kills, contaminated streams/soil), detected toxicants, independent and official testing results, reported health symptoms among residents and responders, and concerns about persistent pollutants (e.g., dioxins).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate measured data (chemical concentrations, sampling results) from anecdotal reports; include study results (e.g., university or atmospheric deposition program findings) and reference exposure limits or health-based guidance when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air and water monitoring results
rubrics_metrics.description: Present findings from EPA, state agencies, and independent researchers on air quality (VOCs, particulate matter) and water testing (presence/absence of vinyl chloride, benzene, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report whether results were above screening or long-term exposure limits, timeframe of sampling, geographic scope, and any disagreements between agencies and independent teams; cite original monitoring reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waste disposal and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how contaminated soil and water were handled, locations of disposal (including out-of-state shipments), notifications to receiving jurisdictions, and any protests or disputes about disposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include tonnage/volumes removed, destinations, and statements from affected jurisdictions; note criticisms about notification and transparency with citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent testing and scientific methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize independent university and research-group sampling campaigns, measurement techniques (e.g., mobile lab van sampling), chemicals detected, and methodological notes (sampling frequency, detection limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the methods and limitations (e.g., mobile sampling every ten feet/second), highlight chemicals of concern, and link to published or publicly released study data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whistleblower and cover-up allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail allegations (e.g., EPA whistleblower claims about delayed aircraft deployment and turning off sensors), responses from agencies, and any evidence presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute allegations to named sources, present official denials or confirmations, and cite FOIA, testimony, or documented records where available; avoid presenting allegations as established facts without corroboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aftermath — company response, cleanup, and commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Document actions and commitments by the railroad (safety plans, removal of contaminated soil/water, compensation pledges), government assistance, town halls, and community outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include timelines, amounts pledged/paid, cleanup milestones (e.g., tons of soil removed), and public statements by officials; cite company disclosures, EPA orders, and official press releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawsuits, legal actions, and compensation programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover class actions, government lawsuits (e.g., DOJ on behalf of EPA), state AG suits, settlement amounts and terms, and compensation programs for homeowners and businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report filing dates, jurisdictions, claims (e.g., Clean Water Act violations), settlement scope (geographic radii, covered harms), and judicial approvals; cite court filings and reputable news/legal reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: NTSB investigation, hearings, and findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe NTSB investigative process, public hearings/field hearings, preliminary and final findings (e.g., cause determination, criticism of the vent-and-burn decision), and any votes or official statements by the board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NTSB reports and hearing transcripts for cause statements and quoted criticism; clearly separate factual findings from board commentary and dissenting opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) safety culture assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize FRA assessments that reference the incident, including findings about handling/analysis of wayside detector data, documentation inaccuracies, safety culture, communication, and procedure consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote or cite the FRA assessment for specific criticisms and recommendations; include any regulatory responses or Calls-to-Action by transportation officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community impact and ongoing local concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on long-term local effects (e.g., resumed hazardous-material trains, resident distrust, health concerns, economic recovery efforts), and local mitigation or monitoring measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include statements from residents, local journalism, recovery/aid programs, and data about ongoing rail traffic; avoid extrapolating unverified long-term health outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inquiry into causes, industry practices, and policy context
rubrics_metrics.description: Place the incident within broader debates (e.g., precision scheduled railroading, reduced crew sizes, regulatory rollbacks like rescinded ECP brake mandate, stock buybacks versus maintenance), and report relevant policy hearings and reform proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute policy critiques to named stakeholders (unions, senators, regulators), cite legislative or regulatory changes, and present counterarguments or company positions to maintain neutrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearings and testimony — detail witness testimony and technical evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Include major hearings, key testimonies (e.g., union officials, academic experts, company representatives), technical evidence presented (hotbox detector data, inspection practices), and expert recommendations (acoustic bearing detectors, inspection protocols).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite hearing transcripts and authoritative testimonies; report technical claims with context and supporting documentation where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain neutral, verifiable sourcing; flag unsourced or disputed statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The article carries maintenance tags such as 'All articles with unsourced statements', 'Articles with disputed statements', and 'All accuracy disputes', indicating the need to ensure claims are verifiable and disputes clearly noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add reliable sources for claims, tag or remove unsourced material, and avoid presenting disputed material as settled. Use reliable secondary sources and official reports for verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive detail and recentism
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial note in the article: 'This section contains an excessive amount of intricate detail. Specifically, too much detail and recentism. Please help improve it by spinning off or relocating relevant information and removing excessive detail that goes against Wikipedia's inclusion policy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condense overly detailed sections, create spin-off articles where warranted (e.g., detailed lawsuits or cleanup timeline), remove recentism that overwhelms encyclopedic balance, and follow Wikipedia inclusion and undue weight policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and formatting conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Page metadata tags: 'Use American English from February 2023' and 'Use mdy dates from February 2023', indicating style conventions for language and date formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt American English spelling and month-day-year date format consistently throughout the article per site conventions; ensure other Wikipedia style guidelines (neutral tone, manual of style) are followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article structure: sections and reference apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: Include standard encyclopedic sections (See also, References, Further reading, External links) and a comprehensive references list supporting statements in the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide inline citations for claims, maintain a references section with full bibliographic details, and use external links judiciously to authoritative sources (EPA, NTSB, peer-reviewed studies).
